To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a novel classification method, called co-clustering based cross-domain classification (CoCC), to learn from in-domain and apply to out-of-domain data; we show that CoCC can achieve high quality classification performance, even when the in-domain and out-of-domain data distributions are different; we present theoretical and experimental analysis to support the findings.

our algorithm can effectively learn the class structure and the class boundary from the in-domain data, and then propagate the learned knowledge to the out-ofdomain data, which is a very difficult task in the machine learning literature.
we have proposed a new co-clustering based algorithm for text classification across domains and have demonstrated its superiority over the traditional algorithms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of learning across different domains, and our proposed algorithm can be applied to many text-mining tasks.
a novel problem of learning across domains.
a new learning paradigm for out-of-domain data classification and we propose a new algorithm for the problem.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CoCC can achieve high classification accuracy for out-of-domain text documents.
the proposed CoCC algorithm is an effective and efficient approach to the problem of classification for out-of-doman data.

CoCC can effectively transfer knowledge from one domain to another and can significantly improve the classification performance for out-of-domain data, even if the distributions between the in-domain and out-of-domain data are different.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, we have developed an effective method to leverage the knowledge from the labeled in-domain data to help improve the classification accuracy of the out-of-domain data.
our CoCC algorithm provides an effective solution to learn from in-domain and apply to out-of-domain, and it is a promising approach to solve the out-of-domain problem in text mining.
we are able to improve classification performance by leveraging unlabeled data from a related domain, even if the distributions are quite different.
The main takeaway from our work is that
co-clustering can be used to bridge two different domains, which can be used to learn from one domain and apply to another.
the co-clustering technique is useful for domain adaptation and can help to solve the out-of-domain problem in text classification.
